sources.news_title: Driver in deadly Kansas soccer field crash released while investigation continues
sources.text:
WICHITA, Kansas (AP) — A woman who drove a pickup truck onto a soccer field during a weekend youth game in Kansas, killing two people and injuring 10 others, has been released without charges as the investigation continues, police said Sunday.
The 34-year-old woman was released pending results of toxicology tests and a mechanical examination of the vehicle in the aftermath of Saturday's crash. Her name hasn't been made public.
“Our officers and investigators will continue working to understand exactly what happened,” Wichita Police Chief Joe Sullivan said, noting that no charges have been filed to date.
The woman had one child playing soccer on another field at the Stryker Sports Complex in northeast Wichita when Saturday's crash occurred, a police statement said. The statement said two of her other children were with her in the pickup truck when it struck multiple children and adults.
According to a preliminary investigation, the Chevrolet pickup was parked in a parking space near the soccer fields before it drove onto one of the fields.
Police identified those killed at the scene as Cole Adrian, 6, and Nicholas Schafer, 35, both of McPherson, Kansas. They were not related.
Ten others ranging from 5 years old to 68 were taken to area hospitals with injuries described as non-serious.
Investigators say they have interviewed more than 30 witnesses, including the driver and her two children who were her inside the pickup at the time of the crash.

BREAKING NEWS – McPherson man, 6-year-old boy killed in Wichita soccer-field crash
Two McPherson residents were killed and 10 people were injured Saturday afternoon after a Chevrolet pickup drove onto soccer fields at Stryker Sports Complex in northeast Wichita, according to the Wichita Police Department.
The victims were identified as 6-year-old Adrian Cole and 35-year-old Nicholas Schafer, both of McPherson. Police said the two were not related and were pronounced dead at the scene.
Sedgwick County 911 began receiving calls at approximately 3:25 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 17, reporting that a vehicle had driven onto soccer fields at Stryker Sports Complex, located at 2999 N. Greenwich Road, and struck several people.
According to the preliminary investigation, the Chevrolet pickup was parked in a parking space near the soccer fields before it drove onto one of the fields, striking multiple children and adults.
As emergency personnel arrived on the west side of the field, witnesses and community members were already providing aid to those injured, police said.
Two juveniles, both children of the driver, were inside the pickup at the time of the crash. The driver also had another child playing soccer on a different field at the complex, according to police.
Ten people injured in the crash were transported to Ascension Via Christi and Wesley Medical Center with injuries described as noncritical. Those injured were a 5-year-old girl, a 5-year-old boy, two 8-year-old boys, a 9-year-old girl, a 28-year-old woman, a 32-year-old man, a 59-year-old woman, a 65-year-old woman and a 68-year-old man.
An additional 61-year-old woman was transported after experiencing medical complications unrelated to traumatic injuries, bringing the total number of people transported to area hospitals to 11.
Investigators interviewed more than 30 witnesses, including the two juveniles who were inside the pickup, before interviewing the driver. Following the interviews, investigators consulted with the Sedgwick County District Attorney’s Office.
The 34-year-old driver from Garden City was released pending the results of toxicology testing and a mechanical examination of the vehicle. No charges have been filed, and investigators continue working to determine the circumstances that led to the crash, police said.
The Wichita Police Department is asking anyone with photos or videos related to the incident to submit them, even if they are unsure whether the footage is relevant to the investigation.
Footage can be submitted through the department’s evidence portal at https://wichitapd.evidence.com/axon/community-request/public/stryker.
Anyone with information about the crash can also contact Wichita police investigators at 316-268-4407. Anonymous tips can be submitted to Crime Stoppers at 316-267-2111.
Police Chief Joe Sullivan expressed condolences to the victims’ families and others affected by the tragedy. The department also thanked community members who stepped forward to help the injured before emergency crews arrived.
The investigation remains active. Police said additional information will be released as it becomes available.

The victims who died were identified as 6-year-old Cole Adrian and 35-year-old Nicholas Schafer, police said. Police originally misidentified the 6-year-old in a release, reversing his first and last name.
An 11th person was also taken to a local hospital after experiencing medical complications unrelated to traumatic injuries, police said.
“This is a tragedy,” Aaron Moses with the Wichita Police Department told reporters outside the complex.
First responders arrived on scene to find community members providing medical aid to those who were injured, Moses said.
‘It was pure panic’
Children were playing soccer on the field with their families gathered nearby when the screeching sound of tires rang out, a video obtained by CNN shows.
The camera of the woman filming the video shakes as she flees the area, with her and others’ screams audible in the recording that appears to capture the moment the truck entered the field.
Vanessa Trammell, who was at the complex watching her 13-year-old son’s soccer game nearby, saw the truck drive across the neighboring field near the sidelines, striking several people, she told CNN.
“It was pure panic,” Trammell said. “I didn’t know what was going on – just that people were being hit. I’m pretty sure I probably screamed, but, absolutely, just pure panic was going through me.”
She added her son’s coach ran to help victims before paramedics arrived at the scene.
One youth player, identified by CNN affiliate KWCH only as Isaac, told the outlet his father was one of the people who rushed to remove the driver from the vehicle.
“My dad went to the truck (and) took the person out of the truck so that they don’t hit any more people,” Isaac said. “(I’m) shocked he did that cause if he didn’t do that, maybe the car wouldn’t have stopped and more people could’ve gotten hit.”

The complex hosts recreational and competitive youth soccer leagues for players ranging from under-5 age groups through high school, as well as adult leagues, according to its website. It has 11 outdoor turf fields and an indoor facility.
Investigators have interviewed more than 30 witnesses at the scene and others over the phone, and have asked for the public’s help as they search for video from the sports complex, Moses said.
All events at the complex have been canceled until further notice, the facility said.
Flag football state championship games scheduled at an adjacent field have also been suspended as police probe the scene, the Kansas State High School Activities Association said in a statement.
Wichita Mayor Lily Wu said she’s “heartbroken” and advised people to avoid the area.
